subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core-owned SecretRef-backed session authentication gate, or keep session tool gating as a plugin/API-extension pattern on before_tool_call?
rationale: This choice defines the permanent security boundary for secret handling, trusted verification, session persistence, reset semantics, transcript redaction, and fail-closed tool execution, so automation should not choose it unilaterally.

options.title: Approve a scoped core gate
options.body: Add a core SecretRef-backed session-auth mode only after specifying verification, redaction, reset behavior, compatibility, and recovery UX.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned
options.body: Use existing before_tool_call hooks plus any needed SDK extension so deployments can opt into session gates outside core.

options.title: Defer the PIN gate
options.body: Keep existing approvals, sandboxing, allowlists, and external-content wrapping as the supported mitigation until a stronger step-up-auth design is selected.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped core gate
recommendation.body: Add a core SecretRef-backed session-auth mode only after specifying verification, redaction, reset behavior, compatibility, and recovery UX.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the implicated session, reset, and tool-policy surfaces and is already in the issue timeline context.
